summary: Develop multi-hazard continuity plans, recovery priorities, and authority coordination skills for essential service providers. Enquire about training.
lede: Business continuity and multi-hazard disaster recovery training for essential services shows you how to turn ISO 22301, ISO 22313, ISO 31000, and the BCI Good Practice Guidelines into workable arrangements. You will connect business impact analysis, hazard scenarios, recovery priorities, critical dependency mapping, crisis coordination, and recovery actions across interconnected operations. Through practical exercises, you will create continuity plans, scenario cards, service continuity registers, recovery decision logs, prioritisation tools, and an exercise programme. You will also use Microsoft Excel templates and a Power BI dashboard structure to track service status and recovery, with overview-level guidance on cyber resilience, service continuity, disaster risk reduction, and public authority coordination.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who maintain essential services, assess operational risk, lead incident response, or coordinate recovery with public authorities. It suits beginner and intermediate practitioners who need an operations-level continuity method, as well as experienced managers who want to strengthen scenario testing and recovery governance.
modules: Business Impact Analysis and Recovery Metrics
Cyber Recovery and Digital Continuity Controls
prerequisites: You should have practical exposure to operations, risk management, emergency preparedness, information technology service management, or business continuity activities. No programming is required, and you do not need prior certification in ISO 22301. Bring a current service map, risk register, continuity plan, or exercise report if organisational confidentiality allows; otherwise, TrainingCred templates and generic datasets support all exercises. Advanced digital topics receive operational application depth. You will configure analysis templates and design dashboard specifications, while production deployment, advanced cyber engineering, and formal certification assessment remain outside the course scope.
